g2.label: 2. Who approves longer working hours on site?

g1.label: 1. agree on the ___ to judge the tenders
g1.why: Criteria are the standards you use to judge or compare options.

g2.label: 2. client, architect and residents are all ___
g2.why: Stakeholders are the people or groups a project or decision affects.

g3.label: 3. only three made it onto the ___
g3.why: A shortlist is the small group of best options chosen from a longer list.

g4.label: 4. gave safety a high ___ in the matrix
g4.why: In a decision matrix, the weighting shows how important a criterion is compared with the others.

g5.label: 5. the ___ we accept to stay on budget
g5.why: A trade-off is something you give up (time) to get something else (a lower cost).

g6.label: 6. the team finally reached a ___
g6.why: You reach a consensus when everyone in a group agrees.

g7.label: 7. 15 November is a ___ we cannot miss
g7.why: A deadline is the latest date by which something must be finished.

g1.label: 1. Everyone on site ___ wear a hard hat (legal requirement)
g1.why: ‘Has to’ expresses an obligation that comes from a rule or law.

g3.label: 3. Workers ___ walk under the crane (dangerous)
g3.why: ‘Mustn't’ means something is not allowed. ‘Don't have to’ would mean it is optional.

g4.label: 4. The new subcontractor ___ be faster (we won't know yet)
g4.why: ‘Might’ expresses a possibility we are not sure about.

g5.label: 5. If the weather stays dry, the frame ___ be finished
g5.why: ‘Ought to’ expresses what we expect to happen if things go to plan.

g6.label: 6. We ___ order more bricks (there are enough)
g6.why: ‘Don't have to’ means it is not necessary. ‘Mustn't’ would mean it is forbidden.
